Preferences
Help
Relays
Follow people to their relays
People publish to relays of their own choosing. When someone you follow uses none of the relays above, the app reads their posts from where they actually publish (their NIP-65 list), read-only, up to six extra relays chosen automatically. Your own list above is never changed.
KEY relays
The relays the KEY itself uses — where it listens for remote signing requests, and what goes into a bunker link it generates. Separate from this app's own relays above. Toggle them on the KEY, or here.
DM inbox relays
Where you receive private messages. Separate from the feed relays above. Saving publishes this list (kind 10050) so other apps know where to reach you — without it, senders guess.
DM relay speed test
Measures connection + round-trip time for each relay. Use the fastest ones for best DM delivery.
Media server
Where photos and videos are uploaded (Blossom). Leave empty to use blossom.primal.net, then the fallback list if it is down.
Secure messages
Loading…
Chats with other Favilla and White Noise users upgrade to forward-secret automatically. They use the Marmot protocol (MLS, RFC 9420, over Nostr): every message has its own key that is deleted after use, so nothing can decrypt it later, not even your seed. Chat keys are stored on this phone encrypted and open only while your KEY is unlocked. Your KEY signs only the key package and the welcome; it never signs chat messages.
Call relays
Call signalling is ephemeral — relays never store it. A call only connects if you and the other person are on a relay at the same moment. Adding relays is safe; the shared defaults are always kept so you stay reachable. Removing them all would make calls fail silently.
Voice & video calls
This page is served from your KEY over plain HTTP, and browsers only grant microphone and camera access to HTTPS pages. So calls open a small secure window that handles ONLY audio and video. Everything else — signing, encryption, relays — happens right here, on your KEY. The call window holds no keys and no pairing.
Call window address
Hosting your own copy of call.html? Point this at it and no Favilla server is involved in your calls at all.
Calls
Calls connect directly between devices whenever the network allows it. When it doesn't — mobile data, restrictive firewalls — the encrypted media is carried by a relay. Favilla runs one, used by default, so calls just work. It cannot decrypt a call, but it does see the addresses of both parties. Run your own to remove Favilla from that position entirely.
Off — maximum compatibility with other Nostr call clients.
Background alerts
Keeps this page awake when it isn't the tab you're looking at, so incoming calls ring and new messages chime even while you're elsewhere. It works by playing a silent tone — that's the only way a browser will let a background page keep running. Costs some battery, and only works while the page is open somewhere: close the browser and nothing arrives.
Muted accounts
Hidden from your feed, notifications and messages; their calls are rejected. Synced to your other Nostr clients (NIP-51).
Muted words
Notes containing any of these words or #tags are hidden from your feeds, Trending and search. Kept on this phone only.
Data usage
Routes images through images.weserv.nl, a free public service that resizes & compresses them — 70-90% less data and much faster loading. That service sees which image addresses you load (not your keys or messages). Turn off to fetch every image straight from its host. Originals load on tap.
QR error correction
Lower = less dense = easier for device camera to scan
Data
Diagnostics
Build —
What each relay delivered and refused, and what the feed kept. Paste it to whoever is helping you debug.
If the app's Content-Security-Policy blocks a script or connection, show a small on-screen notice. For diagnosing issues without a desktop browser's developer console. Off by default.
Writes every relay, call and message diagnostic to the browser console. Off keeps the console quiet, which is lighter on the phone; the feed report still includes the last 300 lines.
If the interface stays frozen for several seconds, reload it. Warns first, and never more than once every five minutes. Calls are always exempt — a reload during a call would end it. On by default; turn it off if you would rather it never reloaded on its own.
Message cache
—
Passwords on your KEY
The KEY keeps each password sealed by its signer chip. This page shows the site and username only: no password ever comes back to the phone. Each change appears on the KEY first; hold ENTER there to save it.
New entries from the KEY
Passwords the KEY made for a new account. Add the site and your username; the password stays as it is.
Entries
Add an entry
Username or email: whichever the site asks for when you sign in. The KEY types it, then Tab, then the password. If the site has both, put the other one in the note.
Recovery codes
The one-time backup codes the site gave you when you turned two-step on. They are sealed on the KEY and shown there one at a time (PASSWORD, UP, UP). Up to 16. Delete them from the site's page or your file once saved.
Import from another password manager
A CSV export from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, 1Password or KeePass, or a Bitwarden JSON export. The file is read on this phone only. You pick the entries; your PIN on the KEY opens its import window, and the KEY seals them one at a time.
Now delete the export file, and empty the trash or Recently Deleted folder it goes to. It holds your passwords in plain text, and anyone who opens it can read them.
Make a QR from a setup key
When a site shows the two-step setup key as letters instead of a QR, type it here. This phone draws the QR; scan it with the KEY (VAULT, Codes, ADD BY QR). The key is not sent anywhere and is wiped when you clear it.
